I'm mapping out the four piece shapes and counting their cells, tallying up to 21 total so far and checking what remains.

I'm testing which piece to remove to hit 16 cells forming a 4x4 rectangle, ruling out the 14-cell (2x7) option since shape widths/heights don't fit, and focusing on removing either the 5-cell or 1-cell shape. I'm working through placing the 7-cell L-shape along one edge of the 4x4 grid, then trying to fit the remaining 5-cell and 4-cell shapes into the leftover cells by testing specific placements.

Trying different offsets for the 5-shape and 4-shape within the remaining region isn't working — the leftover cells keep breaking connectivity. I'm going to try a different placement for the 7-cell shape instead.

Actually, testing removal of shape 5 instead: placing shapes 4, 7, and 1 together, the pieces fit perfectly with the 1-shape and 4-shape filling the remaining region exactly. So the odd one out is shape 5.

content.text:
I'm counting the cells across the four shapes, totaling 22, and testing which piece to remove so the rest could tile a rectangle. Removing the 2 or 5 leaves 17, a prime that can't tile, so I try removing the 6-cell piece instead, leaving 16 cells that could form a 4x4 or 2x8 rectangle, and I'm checking whether the remaining pieces fit that shape.

That configuration leaves an unconnected leftover cell, so that placement fails too. Let me try the 2x8 arrangement instead, checking if the U, 5-piece, and 2-piece can tile it with different column offsets, but the leftover cells keep forming disconnected shapes that don't match the 2-piece's footprint.

Trying to remove 4 pieces instead, leaving 16 cells to cover with the 6-piece, 5-piece, and 5-piece: I'm placing the 6-cell S-shaped piece in the corner of a 4x4 grid and checking what shape remains for the 2-piece to fill.

Still testing placements, but this offset fails too since overlapping cells keep blocking the fit. I'm trying another position for the 6-cell piece across different rows to see if it clears space for the remaining shapes.

Trying the Y-piece and 2-piece placements again, they keep colliding with already-filled cells, so removing 6 or removing 2 from 16 doesn't seem to work either. Since 17 is prime and removal of 4 also failed, I'm stuck checking whether the remaining piece combination can actually tile a 4x4 region at all.

That doesn't work either. Let me re-examine the 2-object and 5-object shapes directly: rows1-2 give a P pentomino, while the 5-object turns out to be an L/J shape with cells at (0,3) and (1,0..3), not the U I assumed. So the pieces to remove are U, P, and L.

Checking the leftover cells after removing U and L: they normalize to (0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2), which is a P pentomino too — matching correctly. That confirms object 6 is the odd one out, forming a distinct 3x3 grid shape.
